articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually drops AWS GovCloud keys on public GitHub like government secrets are Pokemon cards. The agency that's supposed to protect our infrastructure couldn't protect their own lunch money.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: Congress goes full Karen-mode on CISA after their contractor leaked enough secrets to embarrass a three-letter agency. Lawmakers demand answers while we demand better OpSec.

articles.title: State Cyber Leaders Beg Congress for More Funding, Support
articles.summary: TeamPCP unleashes 'Megalodon' malware that devoured 5,500 GitHub repos in six hours like a digital Pac-Man on steroids. Developer credentials got harvested faster than vegetables at a vegan convention.

articles.title: 3 SOC Steps that Shut Down Incident Risks Early
articles.summary: CrowdStrike teams up with Google to takedown GlassWorm's supply chain attack infrastructure. Sometimes the good guys actually win one against the malware peddlers.

articles.title: AI Chatbot Recommendations Redirect Users to Cryptojacking Malware Sites
articles.summary: Gitea vulnerability lets anyone yank private container images without authentication. It's like having a secret vault with a door that opens for literally anyone who knocks.

articles.title: Conifers rolls out AI-powered SOC for unified security operations and automated response
articles.summary: Trend Micro Apex One gets pwned by path traversal bug that's already being exploited in the wild. CISA throws up the warning flags faster than you can say 'zero-day'.

articles.title: EXPOSURE 2026 prepares cybersecurity professionals for the AI era
articles.summary: Anthropic's Claude AI discovers 10,000+ critical vulnerabilities in software systems. When the machines start finding our bugs better than we do, it's time to step up our game.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: EFF exposes how license plate readers have gone full surveillance state - now tracking school residency and noise complaints. Mission creep at its finest, folks.

articles.title: Your Privacy Shouldn't Be A Corporate Decision
articles.summary: Microsoft takes baby steps toward human rights accountability while Google and Amazon pretend they're just neutral cloud providers. At least someone's trying to grow a conscience.

articles.title: ABB Terra AC
articles.summary: TeamPCP's supply chain campaign spreads across three package ecosystems and even infiltrated GitHub's own codebase. These absolute madlads trojaned Microsoft's Python SDK and open-sourced their attack framework.
